items.titleEn: Big Tech's AI bill meets a 'Big Cash Burn' issue: are investors' fears justified?
items.summaryEn: Microsoft is the only hyperscaler in the article showing AI spend translating into both growth and cash: Azure up 48% and free cash flow of $18.6B (about $10B above expectations). The market is punishing “cash burn,” so MSFT should rerate as the cleanest proof that AI capex can still produce shareholder cash. Key Risk: Azure growth slows sharply and free cash flow turns down, proving AI spend isn’t converting into durable returns. Alphabet has strong Cloud demand (Google Cloud revenue $30.71B, more than doubled) but the cash reality is ugly: free cash flow -$9.07B and slowing Search/YouTube ad growth. With investors already worried about Nasdaq 100 cash burn, GOOGL’s negative FCF plus legacy revenue pressure makes it the higher-risk “AI story” versus peers.

items.titleEn: Meta settles, leaving Snap sole defendant in new social media trial
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Meta reached a settlement in a landmark case over the alleged harms of social media, the plaintiffs' lawyers said Friday, leaving Snap as the only defendant in a trial set to open in Los Angeles next week. "We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client," Emily Jeffcott, a lawyer representing one of the young women suing both companies, said in a statement.

items.titleEn: Why AI Investors Are Buying ADT, Accountants and Call Centers
items.summaryEn: Thrive Holdings, an OpenAI-backed holding company, agreed Oct. 29 to buy ADT, the home security provider, for $15.3 billion including debt, a deal that would add 6.1 million monitoring subscribers to a portfolio of more than 75 businesses. Long Lake, the General Catalyst-backed holding company that owns HOA management, payroll and travel businesses, has bought 40 companies, and General Catalyst says its Nexus platform builds board packets in seconds. Lightspeed Venture Partners, the Silicon Valley firm that has backed Anthropic and Databricks, has raised more than $750 million for a fund to buy and upgrade eight to 10 established businesses.

items.titleEn: Anthropic IPO: Blackstone warns AI firm may receive junk credit rating: report
items.summaryEn: Buy the Project North Star junior tranche (the ~$18B double-B-plus, positive-outlook debt). Junk-rated junior paper is where the yield is highest; if the financing structure holds and Broadcom-backed senior debt stays safe, the junior tranche can re-rate upward as rating agencies finalize reviews and investors gain clarity post-IPO. Key Risk: A downgrade to deep junk or a structural cash-flow squeeze that makes junior lease-payment coverage look weak. Sell/avoid ANTHR (Anthropic IPO shares). The news says Blackstone expects a junk (double-B) rating post-IPO, which means higher borrowing costs and a smaller institutional buyer pool for its debt—bad for a company planning massive capex. Even with big cash, the market will price in a higher cost of capital right when it needs funding flexibility.

items.titleEn: Coinbase stock hits two-year low as analyst cuts and Binance hack weigh
items.summaryEn: Sell COIN. Despite an earnings beat, analysts cut targets on weaker crypto trading activity, softer revenue outlook, and higher costs. The stock is already at a two-year low and the market is pricing in continued volume pressure from a broader digital-asset sell-off plus renewed exchange-security fears after the Binance hack. COIN’s “Everything Exchange” progress (prediction markets/USDC) is not enough to offset near-term transaction weakness. Key Risk: Crypto trading volumes rebound fast (BTC/alt rally + risk-on), reversing the revenue outlook cuts and lifting COIN multiples. Sell Circle (CRYPTO-linked exposure via CIRCLE). The article flags stablecoin usage risk if the Binance hack discourages crypto activity. Circle is directly tied to stablecoin flows, so lower stablecoin demand and reduced trading volumes should hit revenue and sentiment harder than broader “exchange” narratives.
